tossups.question: This novel's protagonist beats his wife during the Week of Peace and accidentally kills a clansman, forcing seven years of exile. Its title comes from a (*) Yeats poem, and it ends after Okonkwo hangs himself. For 10 points, name this novel of Igbo life by Chinua Achebe.

According to the Secret History written after his death, this ruler was born clutching a blood clot. Originally named (*) Temujin, he united the steppe tribes in 1206. For 10 points, name this founder of the Mongol Empire.

August Kekule claimed that a dream of a snake biting its own tail revealed this molecule's structure. Its six (*) delocalized pi electrons make it the classic aromatic compound. For 10 points, name this hydrocarbon with formula C6H6, a six-membered carbon ring.

In this novel, the drunkard Marmeladov is trampled by a carriage, and his daughter Sonya follows the protagonist to Siberia. Its main character kills the (*) pawnbroker Alyona Ivanovna with an axe. For 10 points, name this Dostoevsky novel about the student Raskolnikov.

Early in a war, this president suspended habeas corpus along the rail route between Philadelphia and Washington. He delivered a roughly two-minute address at a (*) battlefield cemetery in Pennsylvania. For 10 points, name this president who issued the Emancipation Proclamation and was shot by John Wilkes Booth.

Euclid proved there are infinitely many of these numbers by multiplying a finite list of them and adding one. The sieve of (*) Eratosthenes finds them, and every integer greater than one factors uniquely into them. For 10 points, name these numbers divisible only by one and themselves.

This composer dedicated, then furiously un-dedicated, his third symphony to Napoleon. He premiered his ninth symphony while (*) profoundly deaf, turning around to see the applause he could not hear. For 10 points, name this German composer of the Ode to Joy and a famous fifth symphony.

This figure took the form of a mare to distract a builder's stallion, later giving birth to the eight-legged horse Sleipnir. He engineered the death of (*) Baldr with a mistletoe dart, and he fathered Fenrir and the world serpent. For 10 points, name this Norse trickster god.

This thinker described a pin factory to illustrate the division of labor. He argued that self-interested actors are guided as if by an (*) invisible hand toward the public good. For 10 points, name this Scottish economist who wrote The Wealth of Nations.

Laurens Coster of Haarlem is a disputed claimant to this invention, whose European debut produced a forty-two-line Bible. Its inventor adapted a (*) screw press and cast movable metal type. For 10 points, name this device introduced by Johannes Gutenberg that mechanized book production.

bonuses.leadin: This epic's hero blinds the cyclops Polyphemus. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Greek epic about a long journey home from Troy.
The Odyssey is attributed to this blind poet, also credited with the Iliad.
This faithful wife of Odysseus weaves and unweaves a shroud to put off her suitors.

bonuses.leadin: The Iron Curtain speech announced this conflict's battle lines. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this decades-long standoff between the United States and the Soviet Union.
The Cold War nearly turned hot during this 1962 crisis over Soviet weapons in the Caribbean.
In this 1948 to 1949 operation, Western planes supplied a blockaded city with food and coal.

bonuses.leadin: Rosalind Franklin's Photo 51 helped reveal this molecule's structure. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this molecule that stores genetic information.
These two scientists published DNA's double-helix structure in 1953.
In DNA, adenine pairs with this base.

bonuses.leadin: Only about ten of this poet's nearly eighteen hundred poems were published in her lifetime. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this reclusive poet of Amherst, Massachusetts.
In one Dickinson poem, this personified figure kindly stopped for me in a carriage.
Dickinson wrote that this thing is the thing with feathers that perches in the soul.

bonuses.leadin: This civilization mummified its dead for the journey to the afterlife. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this North African civilization along a great river.
This boy king's nearly intact tomb was found by Howard Carter in 1922.
This stone, inscribed in three scripts, allowed Champollion to decipher hieroglyphs.

bonuses.leadin: An apocryphal falling apple inspired this scientist's theory of gravity. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this English physicist who formulated three laws of motion.
Newton's second law states that force equals mass times this quantity.
Newton and Leibniz independently invented this branch of mathematics.

bonuses.leadin: A bus accident at age eighteen left this painter in lifelong pain. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Mexican painter of The Two Fridas.
Kahlo is best known for many works in this genre, which depict the artist herself.
Kahlo married this Mexican muralist, whose works include Man at the Crossroads.

bonuses.leadin: Souls crossed the river Styx to reach this realm. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Greek underworld, or the god who rules it.
This three-headed dog guards the entrance to the underworld.
This musician nearly retrieved his wife Eurydice from the underworld but looked back too soon.

bonuses.leadin: Dogs salivated at the sound of a bell in this scientist's experiments. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Russian physiologist.
Pavlov's work demonstrated this type of learning, in which a neutral stimulus becomes tied to a reflex.
This American behaviorist studied operant conditioning using namesake boxes.

bonuses.leadin: About half the world's population speaks a language from this family. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this language family that includes English, Hindi, and Russian.
The reconstructed ancestor of the family is abbreviated PIE, short for this name.
This Romance language is the most spoken native language in South America.
